fdroid:com.javimetallab.morselightcrypt.name: MorseLightCrypt
fdroid:com.javimetallab.morselightcrypt.summary: Morse code by light and sound, optionally encrypted. No network.
fdroid:com.javimetallab.morselightcrypt.description:
Send text as Morse code with the flashlight or as beeps, and read it back with the camera or the microphone, optionally encrypted with a master password.
 One phone flashes or beeps, another one watches the light or listens and turns the pulses back into text. It also reads any other blinking light (a lamp, a screen, a torch in the distance) and any Morse tone (a radio, a computer, another phone, an instrument).
 Send : type, pick the speed, choose light, sound or both, and send. Repeat in a loop so the receiver has time to get settled.
 Receive : choose light or sound signal and press Start. Pinch to zoom on distant lights; by ear it finds the sender's pitch by itself. Each repeat lands on its own line, and the received text can be edited by hand.
 Encrypt / Decrypt : AES-256 with a master password, in a compact format of letters and digits made for Morse: "HOLA MUNDO" becomes 26 characters.
 The receiver follows only what blinks, so a bright screen next to the lamp does not blind it, and by ear it follows only the Morse tone, not the noise around it. It measures the sender's speed by itself, tolerates a hand holding the phone and pauses while the phone moves.
 No network permission: nothing leaves the phone except light and sound. The microphone is open only while receiving by sound, and nothing is recorded or stored.
 Sending by light needs a phone with a flashlight; receiving needs a camera or a microphone.
 Available in English, Spanish, Catalan, Galician, Basque, Portuguese, French, German, Italian, Dutch, Polish, Russian, Ukrainian, Chinese, Japanese, Korean, Thai and Hindi.

fdroid:io.keepalive.android.name: Keep Alive
fdroid:io.keepalive.android.summary: Notify others if you haven't used your device in a given period of time
fdroid:io.keepalive.android.description:
Keep Alive will send a custom message via SMS to one or more people if you haven't used your device in a given period of time. Intended to be used as a failsafe for those living alone in case of an accident or other emergency. Once the settings are configured, no further interaction is required.
- 100% Device-based, no cloud services or accounts required
- Free with no ads or trackers
- Open Source (https://github.com/keepalivedev/KeepAlive)
- Minimal Battery Usage
- Multiple SMS Recipients
- Custom Alert Message
- Optional: Include Location Information in SMS
- Optional: Place a phone call with speakerphone enabled
- Optional: Send an HTTP request to a custom URL
Requirements
 Keep Alive requires that your device has an active cellular plan. WiFi calling and messaging will be used if the device supports it.
How it Works
 Keep Alive uses either your device's lock screen or another app(s) to detect activity. If your device hasn't been lock or unlocked for a set period of time, or if you haven't accessed the selected app(s), you will be prompted with an 'Are you there?' notification. If this notification is not acknowledged an Alert will be triggered. Based on the configured Emergency Contact Settings, one or more SMS messages and/or a phone call will be placed to notify others that you may be in need of assistance.
WARNING: If your device restarts, Keep Alive will not be able to check for recent activity until the screen is unlocked. On Android 7.0+, Keep Alive can still send an alert before the screen is unlocked but must assume you have been inactive based on its last saved state. On older Android versions, Keep Alive cannot run at all until the screen is unlocked and alerts will not be sent.
Main Settings
- Monitoring Method - Choose between using the lock screen or another app(s) to detect activity. If using another app(s), you will be prompted to select the app(s) to monitor.
- Hours of Inactivity Before Prompt - how many hours since your phone was last locked or unlocked before you are prompted with an 'Are you there?' notification. Defaults to 12 hours
- Minutes to Wait - if the prompt is not acknowledged within this time, an Alert will be sent based on the configured emergency contact settings. Defaults to 60 minutes
- Rest Period Time Range - a range of time during which inactivity will not be counted. For example, with 'Hours of Inactivity' set at 6 hours and a Rest Period of 22:00 – 6:00, if the device is last used at 18:00, the 'Are you there?' check would not be sent until 8:00. Note that an alert can still be sent during a rest period if the 'Are you there?' check was sent BEFORE the start of a rest period.
- Auto-Restart Monitoring After Alert - If enabled, monitoring will be automatically restarted after an Alert is sent.
- Alert Webhook - Configure an HTTP request to be sent when an Alert is triggered
Emergency Contact Settings
- Phone Call Number (Optional) - when an Alert is triggered a phone call will be placed to this number with speakerphone enabled
One or more SMS recipients can be configured with:
- Phone Number - the phone number to send the Alert SMS to
- Alert Message - the message that will be sent when an Alert is triggered
- Include Location - if enabled, your location will be included in a second SMS
Privacy/Data Collection
No data is collected other than the configured settings and nothing is shared with the developers or any 3rd parties. The only data transmitted is to the configured emergency contacts.
Disclaimer
- Not responsible for SMS or phone call charges incurred by the use of the Keep Alive app
- The operation of the Keep Alive app is dependent on the device, software, and network connectivity. The developers are not responsible for any failure due to device malfunctions, software incompatibilities, or network issues.

hey. i'm spud. i live in the dirt and think about your thoughts sometimes.
spudnote is a notes app for people who are tired of notes apps. no databases, no setup, no folders inside folders inside folders. you open it, you type. that's the whole thing.
here's the part i like: every note you write becomes a little sprout in your field. the ones you tend stay green. the ones you forget grow a small potato hat and wait for you, patiently, no guilt. when a note's done, you pull it up and it drops in the basket. the ones you want to keep close, you pin to a little windowsill shelf. it's calm down here. a snail named gary lives here too. he crawls around visiting your sprouts and leaves a little shiny trail.
what you get:
- open-and-type simplicity. the shortest distance between a thought and a saved note.
- plant from anywhere: share a link or a bit of text from any app, or just tell siri "plant a thought in spudnote".
- a whole field of notes you can actually see, not another gray list.
- rich text when you want it: bold, italic, checklists, the usual. out of the way when you don't.
- fields for the different parts of your life. one for work, one for the garden, one for the 2am ideas.
- a soft soundscape to potter to: a gentle nature bed, the odd rain shower, a little pop when a sprout comes up, and yes, the veggies squeak when you pull them. mute it all whenever you want quiet.
- syncs quietly across your iphone, ipad and mac through your own icloud. i can't read them. nobody can but you.
- widgets that put the field on your home screen: a field at a glance (as sprouts, or a plain list), and a windowsill for the notes you've pinned close. plus a one-tap "plant a thought" button, for when it can't wait.
- a gentle reminder when you want one: tell a note to poke you once, or on repeat for the things that keep coming back. your next one waits on your lock screen, so you see it coming before you even unlock.
no accounts. no ads. no one watching. your notes live in the dirt with me, and the dirt keeps secrets.
spudnote plus:
you start free with two vegetables and two themes to grow in, red boots for the veggies you pull, and a cap, round glasses and a scarf for me. a real notes app, not a trial. keep it that way as long as you like. want the whole garden? plus opens the rest:
- my wardrobe: hats, glasses, a bow tie, a tool belt, a swim ring, even a mustache. dress me up and i'll spin around to show you.
- all vegetable characters to plant and harvest.
- every theme, for whatever mood you're in.
- pastel paint for your sprouts, and it shows up in your widgets too.
- the shed: a little wardrobe out back where you dress up the veggies you pull. sunglasses, a tiny bow tie, a little black suit, whatever suits them.
- the cellar: the pantry stores this month's harvest. the cellar stores every month you've ever pulled, so you can wander back through them.
every october and every december, the season's outfits, its theme and my hat for it are free for everyone.
monthly, yearly, or a one-time forever.

terms of use (eula): https://www.apple.com/legal/internet-services/itunes/dev/stdeula/

that's it. no big pitch. plant a thought, see how it grows.
- spud

fedora-packages:GAPDoc/GAPDoc.description: This package describes a document format for writing GAP documentation. The idea is to define a sufficiently abstract markup language for GAP documentation which can be (relatively easily) converted into different output formats. We used XML to define such a language. This package provides: - Utilities to use the documentation which is written in GAPDoc format with the GAP help system. If you don't want to write your own (package) documentation you can skip to the last point of this list. - The description of a markup language for GAP documentation (which is defined using the XML standard). - Three example documents using this language: The GAPDoc documentation itself, a short example which demonstrates all constructs defined in the GAPDoc language, and a very short example explained in the introduction of the main documentation. - A mechanism for distributing documentation among several files, including source code files. - GAP programs (written by the first named author) which produce from documentation written in the GAPDoc language several document formats: * text format with color markup for onscreen browsing. * LaTeX format and from this PDF- (and DVI)-versions with hyperlinks. * HTML (XHTML 1.0 strict) format for reading with a Web-browser (and many hooks for CSS layout). - Utility GAP programs which are used for the above but can be of independent interest as well: * Unicode strings with translations to and from other encodings * further utilities for manipulating strings * tools for dealing with BibTeX data * another data format BibXMLext for bibliographical data including tools to manipulate/translate them * a tool ComposedDocument for composing documents which are distributed in many files

❤❤❤ Recent reviews : ❤❤❤
- "The best tool to find, close, or switch to the tabs you want, when you have many tabs and windows."
- "Amazingly useful. Can't believe I've spent so much time without a tool like this."
- "In a world of ever-expanding tabs in the browser - this is a helpful addition to keeping them organized and quick switching!"
- "Exactly what I was already looking for the last few months, almost started building it myself :)"
- "This is exactly what I needed. Thanks for putting this together."
If you like it, please leave a review! We read every single review ❤
★ What is Tab Manager Plus?
Tab Manager Plus is a simple and fast Firefox add-on that gives you a clear view of all your open tabs.
You can filter them, move them between windows and organize them in whatever order you like.
Open Tab Manager Plus and start typing right away. Speed is our main priority, so that you can locate the tab you need almost immediately.
★ What you can do:
➤ See all of your tabs and windows together in one overview, instead of clicking through every window separately.
➤ Highlight duplicate tabs. Only the extra copies are selected, and the copy you used last is kept.
➤ Highlight the tabs you used most recently, so you can return to your current activity quickly.
➤ Select several tabs with a right click, or by holding Ctrl, Cmd or Shift while clicking.
➤ Filter your tabs by their title and web address simply by starting to type.
 ➤ Press "Enter" to switch immediately to the tab you found.
 ➤ Press "Enter" to move all highlighted tabs into a new window.
 ➤ Search only titles with t:word, and only web addresses with u:word.
 ➤ Exclude unwanted tabs from the search results by typing -word.
 ➤ Search for an exact phrase by typing "a phrase" inside quotation marks.
 ➤ Search with a /regular expression/ when you need a precise pattern.
 ➤ Search exclusively inside your saved windows by typing s:word.
➤ Switch back to your previous tab with Alt+Shift+Comma (PC) or Ctrl+Shift+Comma (Mac).
➤ Open Tab Manager Plus with Alt+Shift+M (PC) or Ctrl+Shift+M (Mac).
➤ Limit the number of tabs allowed in each window. Once a window reaches its limit, new tabs automatically open in a new window.
➤ Create new tabs and windows directly from the overview.
➤ Move tabs between windows by dragging them to the exact position you want.
➤ Close tabs and whole windows, including saved ones.
➤ Undo deleting a saved window or saved tab with Ctrl+Z (Cmd+Z on a Mac).
➤ Pin and unpin tabs, so important pages stay at the beginning of the window.
➤ Put tabs to sleep so that they use less memory while you are not using them.
➤ See at a glance which tabs are playing audio, muted, sleeping or pinned.
➤ Windows are named automatically after their sites, like GitHub or Gmail, so they are easy to tell apart.
➤ Name and color your windows yourself, and the names and colors remain after Firefox restarts.
➤ Save windows and open them again later, with their original size and position.
➤ Rename and recolor saved windows, and export or import them as a backup.
➤ Drag tabs into saved windows, and move them between saved windows.
➤ Hold the mouse over a tab or window to see more details about it.
➤ Choose a light theme or a dark theme, or let it follow your operating system automatically.
➤ Use it in the Firefox sidebar, in the popup, or in a tab of its own.
➤ Minimize inactive windows: one window stays active, and all the others are minimized.
➤ It works in private windows if you allow it, and the options show you how to do that.
➤ When you save a window, its about:blank tabs are included as well.
➤ "Change shortcut key" in the options opens the Firefox shortcut settings, so you can pick your own keys.
➤ It also works in browsers built on Firefox, like LibreWolf, Zen and Waterfox.
★ Updates
➤ 7.0.0 ( 9th October 2026 )
A brand new look!
- Every layout is new: Block view is a grid, List view shows one tab per line, and Rows view shows one window per row.
- The dark theme has been completely rebuilt, and you can now choose System, Light or Dark. System is the default, because it automatically follows your computer.
- A theme button at the top changes the theme with one click, so you do not need to open the options.
- The add-on comes with redesigned icons and a new collection of colors for your windows.
- Small badges indicate whether a tab is playing audio, muted, sleeping or pinned.
- In List view, small bars show how recently you used each tab, so old tabs are easy to spot.
- The popup opens faster, and typing right after you open it no longer loses the first letters.
Search and duplicates
- Highlight Duplicates selects only the extra copies and keeps the tab you used last, so you can close the rest safely.
- Search for a phrase with quotes, like "pull request", or for a pattern with a /regular expression/.
- A question mark at the right end of the search box opens a list of every available search option.
- A new clock button highlights the tabs you have used most recently. Each additional click reaches a little further back in time.
Windows
- Window names are smarter now, because they use the real names of sites, like GitHub and Gmail.
- Window names and colors stay in place after you restart Firefox, even when their tabs have changed.
- The current window is always listed first, so you can immediately find your position.
- The "switch to previous tab" shortcut works again after being broken in earlier versions.
Saved windows
- Saved windows are now turned on by default, and you can still turn them off in the options.
- You can save just the selected tabs as a new saved window with a single button.
- Click the name or color of a saved window to change it, the same way as for open windows.
- When you open a saved window again, it comes back with its original size and position.
- You can delete saved tabs and windows, and an Undo button stays available for 8 seconds afterwards.
- Drag tabs into saved windows, and drag saved tabs back out into your open windows.
- After an import, a message tells you how many windows were restored and how many were skipped.
- Saved windows no longer have to fit within the browser's 10 MB limit, so you can keep many more of them.
Tab and window info
- Hover over a tab to see when you last used it and what its current state is.
- Hold the mouse over a window to see how many tabs it has, which sites are open and how big it is.
- A small map shows where the window is on your screen.
Options
- The options now list every shortcut key, so you can see at once which keys do what.
- New installations get new default keys: Alt+Shift+M opens Tab Manager Plus, and Alt+Shift+Comma goes to the previous tab. On a Mac, the default keys use Ctrl+Shift instead of Alt+Shift.
- If you do not want them, you can hide the Donate and Rate buttons at the top of the popup.
- You can export your tabs and settings to a file, which helps us when you attach it to a bug report.
Firefox
- "Minimize inactive windows" now works in Firefox, so one window stays active while all the others are minimized.
- The options explain how to allow private windows, and they show whether the add-on is already allowed there.
- "Change shortcut key" opens the Firefox shortcut settings, where you can choose your own keys.
- When you save a window, its about:blank tabs are now kept instead of being left out.
- LibreWolf, Zen and Waterfox are now recognized as Firefox, so the add-on behaves the same way in them.
➤ 6.0.0 ( 1st October 2024 ) open single tabs from saved windows, more reliable closing, moving and restoring
➤ 5.2.4 ( 3rd October 2024 ) backups of large saved sessions, favicons update after loading, sidebar no longer opens on install
➤ 5.2.3 ( 1st October 2024 ) restore saved sessions from the popup
➤ 5.2.1 – 5.2.2 ( 22nd September 2024 ) crash fix for tabs without a hostname or title, permission check fix
➤ 5.2.0 ( 22nd June 2020 ) smarter search with AND / OR, Shift-right click ranges, sidebar panel, bigger popup, blocks by default
➤ 5.1.4 – 5.1.6 ( April 2020 ) moving multiple tabs fixed, window names set the Firefox window title, dark input fields, selectable text again
➤ 5.1.3 ( 4th November 2019 ) popup width adjustable again
➤ 5.1.2 ( 4th November 2019 ) friendlier context menu, speed
➤ 5.1.1 ( 1st November 2019 ) duplicates button back
➤ 5.1.0 ( 31st October 2019 ) sound and sleeping tabs, discard tabs, arrow keys
➤ 5.0.8 ( 28th October 2019 ) backup and restore saved windows, popup or own tab by default
➤ 5.0.7 ( 28th October 2019 ) dark mode
➤ 5.0.4 – 5.0.6 ( October 2019 ) save and restore windows (beta), one permission less, older browsers
➤ 5.0.3 ( 15th August 2019 ) open in its own tab from the context menu
➤ 5.0.0 – 5.0.2 ( 5th August 2019 ) launched for Firefox!
➤ 4.9.0 – 4.9.9 ( 2018 – 2019 ) window colors, auto-hide inactive windows, top sites as window names
Tab Manager Plus is open source, so anyone can read and verify its code.
The main purpose of Tab Manager Plus is to help you rediscover tabs you have lost. Open it with Alt+Shift+M (PC) or Ctrl+Shift+M (Mac), or click its icon, and then start typing right away.
It immediately shows every tab whose title or web address matches the words you entered.
When the tab you were looking for is the only one selected, press "Enter" to jump directly to it.
There are 4 layouts:
★ Block view ( one group of icons for each window )
★ Big block view ( the same, with bigger icons )
★ Rows view ( one line for each window, one icon for each tab )
★ List view ( a list of all your tabs, with readable titles )
You can move tabs between windows in every layout.
Select individual tabs with the right mouse button, or with Ctrl+click on a Mac.
Then press "Enter" to move all of the selected tabs into a new window.

Adds a dark theme to the LMS DayMap used by South Australian public schools.
This extension adds a dark theme to the LMS used by public schools in South Australia (DayMap). If you are sick of the white theme just download and install this extension!
If you find any bugs feel free to report them, either via email, via the support tab or github.
Open Source at: https://github.com/Gabriel-06/Daymap-Dark-Theme

apple-macos:6739386670.description:
Termix is a modern SSH client and terminal developed by a European team of cybersecurity experts. It offers an unrivaled SSH and SFTP experience that enhances your productivity without compromising your privacy.
With zero ads and a strict no-data-collection policy, Termix uses the most secure open-source libraries to keep your connections safe.
Key Features:
Ultimate SSH & SFTP Client:
Termix delivers a robust, desktop-grade terminal experience across all Apple devices.
Advanced File Manager & Code Editor:
Inspired by WinSCP, our fully featured file manager lets you download, upload, manage, and edit files, directories, and permissions effortlessly. It also includes a rich code editor with syntax highlighting that supports over 40 programming languages.
Native Gestures & Keyboard Shortcuts:
Navigate like a pro with native touch gestures and hardware keyboard shortcuts, enabling fast navigation, multiline command editing, and precise text selection. Termix feels just like a regular text editor with all the perks you need for efficient terminal work.
Multi-Session & Customization:
Work in parallel with seamless split-screen support, advanced key management (including generation and uploading), and a fully customizable interface with themes tailored for power users.
Serverless Security:
Termix works completely serverless. All your hosts, private keys, and passwords are stored in encrypted form on Apple iCloud and never leave your device. This design guarantees that your sensitive data remains exclusively under your control.
Enhanced Automation:
Boost your workflow with startup snippets, execute commands across multiple hosts simultaneously, and configure environment variables with ease.
Modern Apple-Native Design:
Experience a clean, smooth, and beautifully modern interface designed exclusively for Apple products.
Developer & Sysadmin Focused:
Built for developers and loved by system administrators, Termix includes features such as command history, regex search, and snippet support to save hours of time and increase productivity.
With Termix Pro, you can also:
- Upload and edit files using the File Manager.
- Create startup snippets.
- Execute snippets on multiple hosts simultaneously.
- Import custom fonts.
- Manage and configure environment variables. 
- Choose an alternative icon for Termix.
Discover the most powerful, secure, and feature-rich SSH and SFTP client made for those who demand quality. Get Termix today and transform your remote management experience!

firefox-addons:2717093.summary: Max HackBar is a Firefox WebExtension by Mr. Bipolar, inspired by the original HackBar. It offers SQL injection, encoding, hashing and HTTP testing tools directly in Firefox Developer Tools.
firefox-addons:2717093.description:
Max HackBar is a Firefox WebExtension inspired by the original HackBar and developed as an alternative to its legacy XUL-based version.
It provides a convenient collection of tools for web developers, penetration testers, and security researchers to perform web security testing and inspect HTTP requests and responses directly from Firefox Developer Tools.
 Open Firefox.
 Press F12 to open Firefox Developer Tools.
 Select the HackBar tab.
 Choose a tool and use it for your testing.
 SQL Injection: Ready-to-use SQL injection testing payloads and utilities.
 Encoding and Decoding: URL encoding, Base64 encoding/decoding, ROT13 and string/HEX conversion.
 Hashing: MD5, SHA-1 and SHA-256.
 HTTP Requests: GET and POST request testing.
 Custom Requests: Configure request headers and request data.
 Response Inspection: View responses from your testing requests.
 Developer Tools Integration: Access HackBar directly within Firefox Developer Tools.
Max HackBar does not require an account or registration.
 Public IP Information 
The extension automatically contacts ipinfo.io to retrieve your public IP address and associated country information for display in the HackBar panel.
A third-party service is required to determine the public IP address visible to the internet. This request exposes your public IP address to ipinfo.io , which processes the request and returns IP-related information.
 Web Testing Requests 
When you use HTTP or security testing features, the extension sends the URLs, request headers and request data you provide to the selected target website. It also reads the responses so you can inspect the results.
These network requests are necessary for the testing functionality. Only test websites and systems that you own or have permission to assess.
The extension does not use these features for advertising or unrelated analytics.
Max HackBar is an open-source project. You can explore the source code, report issues and contribute through GitHub:
 Max HackBar – GitHub Repository 
Feedback and contributions are welcome.
